Every count below was MEASURED against the pre-port monolith and is IDENTICAL there (execute 62/243, node_status 23/146, manifest_errors 32/124, resource_edges 18, checkpoint 22, cancel 15, merge_lane 13) — the move added not one branch, and the byte-identical bodies make that checkable rather than assertable. The R-RET-03 stage-1 skill pin, restored by task 49 into `retrieval.pinpolicy` so all THREE call sites share one implementation. Measured against the monolith: 22 branches there, 22 here — the move added none. The branch count IS the learnings-eviction guarantee: the naive pin is a two-line pop-and-insert, and everything above that count is the machinery that stops the insert pushing a LEARNING out of the surfaced window to make room for a procedure. R-RET-03 guarantees learnings are always included precisely because they carry prior problems and errors, so silently dropping one at a small top-k is the failure this code exists to prevent — and it is a failure with no visible symptom, since the caller just sees a shorter list it never counted. Decomposing it would spread one guarantee across helpers whose individual correctness says nothing about whether the guarantee holds. Owned by task 67 with the rest of the residual.

The vetted skill INSTALL GATE, ported by task 54 as a pure move. Both counts are IDENTICAL in the pre-port monolith (reconcile 26, cmd_skill_sync 34) — the move added no branch. These two are also the functions where a decomposition is most likely to introduce the one bug this subsystem may not have: `--approve` is the ONLY path that installs a skill where a harness will EXECUTE it, and every branch in `_skill_reconcile` is one arm of the verdict table (installed / pending / changed-since-approval / blocked / foreign / shadowing a package skill / removed from the KB). Quarantine-on-change lives in those arms: approval binds to a CONTENT HASH, so a skill whose tree changed returns to PENDING rather than carrying the old approval forward — because the operator approved a body, not a title, and the second version is the one worth attacking precisely because the first was reviewed. `cmd_skill_sync` (34) is the mode dispatcher over that table: approve / reject / uninstall / reset / status / status-line, each with its own refusal conditions. Splitting either in the same commit that moves it is exactly the concentrated risk the ratchet prevents. Owned by task 67 with the rest of the residual.
